title: Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance Meteorite: Calibre ARF22 In Steel
excerpt: Armin Strom unveils the Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite in stainless steel. 39mm case, calibre ARF22, limited to 15 pieces at CHF 105,000.
content:
Armin Strom unveils the Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite, a rare 15-piece limited series that pairs the manufacture’s patented resonance clutch mechanism with dual dials sculpted from genuine extraterrestrial meteorite. Encased in a refined 39.00 mm stainless steel chassis measuring an ultra-slender 9.05 mm in height, the timepiece houses the manual-winding manufacture Calibre ARF22. Operating two entirely independent balance wheels synchronized by physical resonance at 25,200 vibrations per hour (3.5 Hz), this horological achievement delivers dual completely autonomous time zones, twin 3D-engraved day/night indicators, and 42 hours of autonomy.

We begin with our commentary and analysis, followed by the complete official Armin Strom press release.

Price, Specifications & Official Press Release

The Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite retails for CHF 105,000 (excluding taxes) in a limited edition of 15 pieces worldwide.

Deployant’s Commentary & Analysis

The technical core of the timepiece is manufacture Calibre ARF22, a movement engineered to solve the 200-year-old horological conundrum of sustaining a persistent resonance state in a wrist-worn environment. While classical watchmakers like Abraham-Louis Breguet and modern masters like François-Paul Journe relied strictly on acoustic and aerodynamical coupling across tight spatial proximity, Armin Strom co-founder and technical director Claude Greisler devised a patented resonance clutch spring made from steel. This flexible bypass link directly bridges the outer stud terminals of the two balance springs, transferring kinetic vibrations between the balance wheels in real time. If a physical shock upsets one oscillator, the clutch spring forces both back into synchronous opposition within seconds, dramatically mitigating rate deviations and conferring unmatched chronometric stability.


Visually, the Manufacture Edition Meteorite departs from the grenage and aventurine executions of earlier editions by adopting natural iron-nickel meteorite for both dials. Sliced from genuine meteorite and acid-etched to highlight its signature Widmanstätten crystalline cross-hatch structures, no two dials possess the same geometric pattern, rendering each of the 15 timepieces unique. Framing the meteorite fields are black azurage chapter rings with faceted, polished rose gold-coated applied indices and matching faceted rose gold hands. This subtle infusion of warmth prevents the watch from feeling starkly monochromatic, establishing a harmonious contrast against the polished stainless steel case and anthracite plate backgrounds.


Housed within a 39.00 mm diameter stainless steel case with an overall lug-to-lug span of 44.50 mm and an extraordinarily slim profile of just 9.05 mm, this iteration represents the peak of wearable high horology. Compressing a complex dual-movement architecture into sub-10mm proportions required Armin Strom to arrange the regulating organs vertically along the 12-to-6 axis, placing the twin balance assemblies under open sapphire view while tucking the gear trains beneath. Dual dedicated crowns flank the case at 4 o’clock and 8 o’clock, allowing the wearer to set each time zone completely independently down to the minute. This architecture effortlessly accommodates unusual non-standard half-hour (such as India and Adelaide) and quarter-hour time zones (such as Nepal and the Chatham Islands), while maintaining an everyday water resistance of 50 metres (5 ATM).


Beneath the twin dials, the ARF22 displays two dedicated day/night rotating discs finished in blackened and mirror-polished steel, providing immediate AM/PM orientation for both local and home time. Winding the watch via the right crown energizes twin mainspring barrels equipped with slipsprings that prevent over-tensioning once the 42-hour autonomy is achieved. The decoration reflects the manufacture’s commitment to hand-finishing: every steel component is assembled twice, displaying meticulous hand-bevelled and mirror-polished anglage, straight graining, circular graining (perlage), and mirror-black polished screw heads. The watch is presented on a supple matte grey alligator strap with tone-on-tone grey stitching, secured by a stainless steel pin buckle.

Pricing notes

Priced at CHF 105,000 (excluding taxes), the Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite commands a high-entry ticket reflecting its extreme rarity and complex proprietary manufacture construction. Within the exclusive universe of resonance wristwatches, its only direct conceptual peer is the F.P. Journe Chronomètre à Résonance, which trades on the secondary market between CHF 200,000 and CHF 350,000 depending on reference and alloy. Given that earlier Armin Strom 39 mm resonance editions in 18k white gold and rose gold debuted at CHF 59,000 to CHF 63,000 with grenage dials, the meteorite execution carries a substantial premium for its natural extraterrestrial material, stainless steel exclusivity, and microscopic 15-piece worldwide allocation. For collectors seeking an uncompromising blend of genuine chronometric innovation, wearable dimensions, and cosmological provenance, this edition stands in a league of its own.

Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite Specifications

  • Model: Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite
  • Reference: ST26-DT.MT
  • Limitation: Limited edition of 15 pieces worldwide
  • Case: Stainless steel; sapphire crystal and exhibition caseback with anti-reflective treatment; dual setting crowns at 4 o’clock and 8 o’clock
  • Dimensions: Diameter 39.00 mm; height 9.05 mm; lug-to-lug distance 44.50 mm
  • Water Resistance: 5 ATM (50 metres / 165 feet)
  • Dials: Twin natural meteorite dials with unique Widmanstätten crystalline patterns; black azurage chapter rings; applied rose gold-coated polished indices; polished and blackened steel day/night indicator discs
  • Hands: Rose gold-coated, facetted and mirror-polished
  • Functions: Dual independent time zones (hours, minutes) with separate day/night AM/PM indicators; patented resonance clutch mechanism; GMT functionality
  • Movement: Armin Strom manufacture Calibre ARF22; manual winding; two independent regulating systems interconnected by a patented resonance clutch spring; dual mainspring barrels with slipsprings
  • Movement Dimensions: Diameter 34.15 mm; thickness 4.92 mm
  • Frequency: 25,200 vibrations per hour (3.5 Hz)
  • Jewels: 40 jewels
  • Component Count: 231 components
  • Power Reserve: 42 hours
  • Finishing: Movement assembled twice; hand-bevelled and polished bridges, circular graining (perlage), straight graining, black-polished steel screws and chatons
  • Strap & Buckle: Matte grey alligator leather strap with tone-on-tone grey stitching; stainless steel pin buckle
  • Price: CHF 105,000 (excluding taxes) / approx. USD 118,000
  • Availability: Immediate release via authorized retailers and Armin Strom boutiques

For further reading and previous coverage of Armin Strom’s resonance innovations, see our hands-on review of the Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance in 39mm, the earlier Dual Time Resonance Masterpiece 1, the Dual Time Resonance GMT release, and the Mirrored Force Resonance First Edition.

The Official Press Release

Not of This World. Very Much in Its Element.

A Natural Choice.

Some materials don’t need much help making an impression. Meteorite is one of them. For this edition of the Dual Time GMT Resonance, Armin Strom has chosen natural meteorite for both dials, allowing the stone’s own texture and shades of grey to set the tone. Its naturally occurring colour complements the stainless steel case, creating an almost monochromatic look in which the different surfaces work together rather than compete for attention. Rose gold coloured hands and indexes provide just enough warmth to break up the grey, without taking anything away from the meteorite.

And because meteorite is a natural material, no two dials will have exactly the same pattern. Each watch carries a detail that cannot be reproduced by design.

The Science of Staying in Sync.

The manual-winding manufacture calibre ARF22 is entirely designed, developed and produced in-house by Armin Strom. Its patented resonance clutch connects two independent regulating systems, allowing the balance wheels to synchronise through the physical phenomenon of resonance. This continuous interaction improves chronometric stability, turning a scientific principle into a practical advantage on the wrist.

Each time zone has its own hours, minutes and day/night indicator, allowing two different times to be read independently. Operating at 3.5 Hz (25,200 vph) and offering a 42-hour power reserve, the ARF22 combines Armin Strom’s approach to resonance with a complication designed for everyday use.

Nature Has Its Patterns. So Do We.

The movement tells a different story of craftsmanship. Complementing the natural patterns of the two dials, the carefully decorated components reveal the work carried out by Armin Strom’s watchmakers. Hand-bevelled and polished edges, black-polished screws, perlage and circular graining reflect the traditional decoration of the movement. Nature takes care of the pattern. Armin Strom takes care of the precision. Every Armin Strom watch is assembled twice – once to make it work, and once to make sure it works exactly as it should.

From outer space. Down to 15 pieces on Earth.
